translate_en|mods/Blackout Predators/42/: Maximum number of the 572 fixed nest locations enabled in this world. A stable, map-wide subset is selected; inactive fixed nests do not spawn Volatiles or run nest processing. 0 disables fixed nests but does not disable ambient Volatile spawns. Lower values reduce CPU use and maximum nest population. Default: 572.
Chance for each normal zombie encountered at night to become a roaming Volatile. 0 disables ambient Volatile spawns. Default: 9%%.
Hour when outdoor Volatile spawning stops and they return to their nests. The fixed 2× XP bonus also ends at this hour. Default: 06:00.
Maximum number of Volatiles assigned to each nest. Default: 7.
Minimum number of Volatiles assigned to each nest. Default: 4.
Hour when Volatiles begin spawning and hunting outdoors. The fixed 2× XP bonus also begins at this hour. Default: 00:00.
When enabled, active purple-bulb lamps repel Volatiles. Disable this to stop UV-light scans, reports and reactions and reduce performance cost for the entire world/server. Default: Enabled.
Total health assigned to each Volatile. Default: 12.
Distance at which each Volatile can hear players and sounds. Does not change ordinary zombies. Default: Pinpoint.
How long each Volatile remembers a player after seeing or hearing them. Does not change ordinary zombies. Default: Long.
Distance at which each Volatile can see players. Does not change ordinary zombies. Default: Eagle.
Direct animation and movement scale. Normal Sprinter: 0.80. Default: 0.96 (about 20%% faster). Range: 0.40-1.60.
Damage inflicted by each Volatile per attack. Does not change ordinary zombies. Default: Superhuman.

Volatile hours follow the world's Sandbox settings (00:00–06:00 by default). At night, Volatiles wake, leave buildings and hunt outdoors. <LINE> <LINE> Volatiles are fast, tough and highly alert. All skill XP gained during Volatile hours is doubled. <LINE> <LINE> When you hear their screams, find shelter or prepare an escape route.

Outside Volatile hours, Volatiles sleep inside buildings. Their heavy breathing can reveal a nest. <LINE> <LINE> A sleeping Volatile may wake if you approach, make noise nearby or hit it. <LINE> <LINE> During the day it may attack an intruder inside the building, but it will not continue the chase outside. Listen, stay quiet and keep an escape route.

At night, a switched-on lamp fitted with a purple bulb acts as a UV light. Handheld flashlights are not UV sources. <LINE> <LINE> UV forces nearby Volatiles to stop attacking and flee from the light. It does not damage or kill them; it creates only temporary space. <LINE> <LINE> Keep the lamp powered and switched on. If Enable UV Mechanics is disabled in Sandbox settings, purple-bulb lamps have no effect.

You can customize Volatile difficulty, hunting hours, encounters, nests and UV mechanics under Sandbox > Blackout Predators. <LINE> <LINE> Lower settings can reduce the performance cost on busy worlds and multiplayer servers. <LINE> <LINE> For low-end systems, disable UV mechanics and set Active Nest Limit to 0. You can also lower Ambient Volatile Spawn Rate if you want fewer nighttime encounters.

Sets the minimum delay between ambient Volatile screams while no player is detected. Higher values make the night quieter. Chase and attack vocals remain more frequent after a Volatile detects a player. Default: 60 seconds.
Opens the Blackout Predators tutorial while a game is loaded. New characters see it automatically once.
Adjusts Blackout Predators' custom Volatile sounds for this client. 0%% mutes them, 100%% keeps the default volume, and 200%% doubles it. The game's main sound settings still apply.
